summary: The milestone completed 5 experiments in 0.2 minutes, with 1 compute-bound task. Bounded ARC local-generation liveness and receipt recovery is recorded at 0.0 minutes, so the supplied data exposes no compute-duration bottleneck; the locked compute-task GPU-idle indicator is false.
bottlenecks_identified: Disk-mtime reconstruction and 0.0-minute recording obscure the phase cost of the compute-bound task; this is an observability bottleneck, not evidence of slow execution.
The GPU monitor snapshot is not correlated to the compute-bound task window, so accelerator efficiency during that task cannot be determined.
No data available this milestone establishes a 2+ model parallel task or records its runner choice, so a missed DualGPURunner dispatch cannot be evaluated.
improvements_suggested: Emit monotonic experiment start, end, and per-phase durations at sub-minute precision instead of relying only on disk-mtime reconstruction.
Attach timestamped GPU utilization and memory samples to each compute-bound task window.
Write launch receipts with model count and selected runner, and select DualGPURunner only for tasks that load 2+ models in parallel.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add sub-minute, per-phase monotonic timing receipts for every experiment.
Correlate GPU samples with the compute-bound task start and end times.
Record launch-time model count and runner selection so DualGPURunner eligibility is auditable.
meta_reflection: The 0.2-minute milestone and 0.0-minute compute entry do not support a positive speedup claim. Higher-resolution task-linked timing, GPU, and dispatch receipts are needed to distinguish efficient execution from missing observability in the next retrospective.
